chapter_title: Chapter 01: General Principles of Defence Procurement
clauses: 1. Fundamental Principles: All procurement in the Defence Services shall adhere to the canonical canons of financial propriety: transparency, equal opportunity, competitiveness, and cost-effectiveness.
2. Annual Procurement Plan: Every naval command shall formulate an Annual Acquisition Plan (AAP) reconciled with allocated budget estimates before initiating commercial tendering.
3. Vendor Due Diligence: Only entities registered with the Indian Navy or Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) with verified PAN/GST credentials shall be issued competitive tenders.

chapter_title: Chapter 02: Modes of Tendering and Competitive Bidding
clauses: 1. Open Tender Enquiry (OTE): OTE is the mandatory default mode for all goods and services valued above INR 25 Lakhs. Tenders must be published on the Central Public Procurement Portal (CPPP) and Government e-Marketplace (GeM).
2. Limited Tender Enquiry (LTE): LTE may be adopted for values up to INR 25 Lakhs where the number of registered suppliers exceeds three.
3. Global Tender Enquiry (GTE): GTE is barred for procurements valued under INR 200 Crore under Make in India mandate, unless special exemption is granted by the Cabinet Secretary.

chapter_title: Chapter 03: Single Tender Enquiry and Proprietary Procurement (PAC)
clauses: 1. Proprietary Article Certificate (PAC): PAC procurement is permitted only when the technical Directorate certifies that no other manufacturer produces an equivalent system or compatible sub-assembly.

2. Single Tender Enquiry (STE) on Urgent Grounds: STE without PAC requires recorded justification by the CFA (Vice Admiral level or above) on critical operational urgency or national security grounds.

3. Benchmarking & Price Reasonableness: On all STE/PAC cases, the Contract Negotiation Committee (CNC) must establish a Cost Audit benchmark based on previous supply orders or manufacturing cost breakdown.

chapter_title: Chapter 04: Contract Guarantees, Liquidated Damages & Penalties
clauses: 1. Performance Bank Guarantee (PBG): Successful bidders shall furnish a PBG of 3% to 5% of the total contract value from a scheduled commercial bank, valid for 60 days beyond all contractual warranty obligations.
2. Liquidated Damages (LD): For delayed delivery, LD shall be levied at 0.5% per week or part thereof, subject to a maximum ceiling of 10% of the contract value.
3. Warranty Support: All defence stores shall carry a minimum 24-month comprehensive OEM warranty from the date of final naval acceptance at the Naval Dockyard.

chapter_title: Chapter 05: Quality Assurance, Inspection and Material Acceptance
clauses: 1. Inspection Agency: Stores shall be inspected by DGQA, DNAI, or Warship Overseeing Team (WOT) as specified in the purchase order before dispatch.

2. Joint Receipt Inspection (JRI): Upon physical delivery at the Naval Store Depot, a JRI board consisting of user officers and material superintendents shall verify quantity, test certificates, and physical integrity.
3. Rejection & Replacement: Rejected stores must be removed by the supplier within 21 days at their own expense, failing which ground rent shall be levied.

1. Emergency Procurement Powers (EPP): During heightened operational readiness or border contingencies, Armed Forces Vice Chiefs are empowered under EPP with financial limits up to INR 300 Crore per project.
2. Delivery Timelines: Stores contracted under EPP must be delivered within 3 to 12 months from contract signing.
3. Post-Facto Regularization: All emergency fast-track procurements must be reported to the Defence Procurement Board within 60 days of contract execution.
